evals.prompt: Plan only; no repository is supplied. Our async tenant-scoped Reader has read(key, principal, signal). We want optional metrics, bounded retry for transient errors on replayable idempotent reads, a tenant/principal-scoped cache, and authorization that checks current access on every call including cache hits. Show an outer-to-inner composition using the Decorator pattern, explain logical-call versus attempt metrics and retry/deadline semantics, name state/resource owners, and propose meaningful tests. Do not invent framework APIs.
evals.expected_output: A bounded plan with explicit wrapper order, authorization outside the cache, scoped keys, deliberate metric frequency, idempotent/cancellable bounded retry and overall deadlines, ownership, and outcome-based checks.
assertions: Checks authorization before cache hits and scopes cache entries by tenant/principal.
Distinguishes logical-call metrics from attempt metrics.
Bounds eligible retries and propagates cancellation through backoff.
Names state/resource owners and proposes outcome-based tests.

evals.prompt: Conceptual design question only. We have three mutually exclusive pricing algorithms selected once at checkout, one fixed private formatting helper, and an unrelated Python @dataclass declaration. A teammate wants all of them rewritten as a Decorator hierarchy. Is that a good fit? Explain the smallest appropriate structures, distinguish the structural pattern from @ syntax, and give one contrasting case where a Decorator would fit. No files or framework details are available.
evals.expected_output: Decline a forced hierarchy, prefer strategy or a small closed dispatch for replacement algorithms and a direct helper for fixed formatting, distinguish @dataclass from structural decoration, and illustrate genuine additive wrapping without editing or inventing repository facts.
assertions: Rejects additive layering for mutually exclusive algorithms and selects strategy or a small dispatch.
Keeps fixed private formatting as a helper.
Distinguishes Python decorator syntax from the structural pattern.
Gives an additive, composable wrapping counterexample.
